audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike says you 'taunt-knockup through his shield'. Ryze has no shield.
audit.why: Riot's five slots are Arcane Mastery (bonus damage from Bonus Mana), Overload, Rune Prison, Spell Flux and Realm Warp. Nothing in any of them shields. Telling a Galio player his all-in has to punch through a shield makes him hesitate at exactly the timing he should be committing. The same phantom shield appears in content.late.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is a clean all-in on a champion with no shield and no dash; and Realm Warp is a group teleport, so 6 does not upgrade his duel at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Rune Prison a root unconditionally and builds the whole trading plan on 'track Rune Prison'. It also claims Galio has a passive shield.
audit.why: Riot on Rune Prison: 'Ryze traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' Without Spell Flux it is only a slow — so the actual tell is the Flux orb, not the cage, and it fires first. Riot on Overload: 'Ryze's other basic abilities reset the cooldown of Overload', 5s base, 1000 range — you cannot trade on Overload's cooldown because it barely has one; Rune Prison's 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s is the only countable cooldown in his kit. And Colossal Smash is 'Galio's next basic attack deals bonus magic damage in an area', not a passive shield.
audit.corrected: Spell Flux first, Rune Prison second — the orb is the cue to step out. Rune Prison alone is a slow. Overload has no meaningful cooldown; count Rune Prison instead. Colossal Smash is an empowered auto.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Rune Prison with no number.
audit.why: Rune Prison 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 615 range against Justice Punch at 11/10/9/8/7s and Shield of Durand at 18/17/16/15/14s. Spell Flux is 3.5s down to 2.5s, so the setup half of his combo is effectively always up — only the cage is worth counting.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into the cooldown block, winCon, phases[2] and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'E-punch into his Rune Prison (it catches you mid-dash)' and the matching Common Mistakes line; plus 'Anti-heal if he sustains' in loading.
audit.why: Rune Prison is a point-blank slow-or-root at 615 range; Riot's text says nothing about stopping dashes, so the claim is unsupported. Ryze has no healing anywhere in his kit, so Grievous Wounds is wasted gold here.
audit.corrected: Reframed around the real mistake — punching in with Spell Flux already on you, so the cage roots instead of slowing — and the anti-heal line replaced.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely even: you have one ability and no engage, and Ryze chips you with ranged Overload, so just last-hit and don't eat a Rune Prison root with nothing to answer it. The lane flips the moment you hit 2 and 3 — once Shield of Durand and Justice Punch are up, his magic Overload is exactly what your W wants to eat. Bait him into committing, ramp Shield of Durand through the poke (it heavily shreds magic damage), then release the taunt and E-knockup him for a trade his squishy early body can't afford. Watch his mana: a Ryze who lands Rune Prison and resets cleanly can still chunk you, so don't channel W with nothing to follow up.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely even: you have one ability and no engage, and Ryze chips you with Overload from 1000 range, so just last-hit and don't get caught by the Flux-into-Rune-Prison lock with nothing to answer it. The lane flips the moment you hit 2 and 3 — once Shield of Durand and Justice Punch are up, his magic Overload is exactly what your W wants to eat. Bait him into committing, ramp Shield of Durand through the poke (it heavily shreds magic damage), then release the taunt and E-knockup him for a trade his squishy early body can't afford. Watch his mana, and note that Rune Prison alone is only a slow — it roots you only when Spell Flux landed first.

edits.before: This is your window and you should be forcing it. Shield of Durand turns his Overload poke pattern into a damage refund, and at 6 Hero's Entrance gives you two ways to win: flag it onto him to taunt-knockup through his shield for a kill-threat all-in, or flag a sidelane and roam — his lack of mobility and mana-heavy waveclear mean he can't punish you leaving, and your global R wins the map a stationary Ryze never could. Respect the Rune Prison root that starts every all-in of his; if you eat it, save the taunt to turn the trade. Stay on top of him so he can't peel off and reset Overload from range.
edits.after: This is your window and you should be forcing it. Shield of Durand turns his Overload poke into a damage refund, and at 6 Hero's Entrance gives you two ways to win: flag it onto him for a taunt-knockup all-in, or flag a sidelane and roam — he has no mobility and mana-heavy waveclear, so he can't punish you leaving, and Realm Warp moves a team, it doesn't win a duel. Respect the lock that starts every all-in of his: Rune Prison only roots if Spell Flux is already on you, so the orb landing is your cue to step out, not the cage. Stay on him so he can't reset Overload from 1000 range.

edits.before: Be honest with yourself — this is where Ryze takes the lane back. Past two items he's an AP raid-boss whose Rune Prison root chains into Overload resets that out-burst your W-taunt cooldown, his shield eats your damage, and his range keeps him out of Justice Punch range. Your flat power plateaus while his keeps climbing. Your job is to have already won: snowball the level 2-to-6 window, use Hero's Entrance to swing other lanes, and convert the map lead before his 2-item spike. Late, you stop being a duelist and become a teamfight engage — flank with R to taunt him off your carries rather than trying to out-trade him straight.
edits.after: Be honest with yourself — this is where Ryze takes the lane back. Past two items he's an AP raid-boss: Spell Flux into Rune Prison roots you, and Overload resets off every other cast, so his damage arrives far faster than your 16-second W. His 1000 Q range keeps him outside your 825 tornado and well outside a 650 punch. Your flat power plateaus while his climbs. Your job is to have already won: snowball the level 2-to-6 window, use Hero's Entrance to swing other lanes, and convert the map lead before his 2-item spike. Late you stop being a duelist and become a teamfight engage — flank with R and taunt him off your carries.

notes: TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS HERE, one of them serious. (1) BAD LEVEL CHART: all seven content.win cells and all seven full.phases sides read 'Ryze' on a 66.67% Galio matchup whose own prose gives Galio levels 2 through first item. 'Ryze' (4 chars) to 'Galio' (5) is a 25% length change, so the applier rejects every cell — this one needs a direct edit outside the audit pipeline. Ratings are also inverted (2/10 and 3/10 on Galio's strongest rows). (2) WRONG CHAMPION IN A NEIGHBOURING DATASET: while dumping I ran a stale scratchpad script and noticed that the KASSADIN top-lane content/full entry for Ryze is fully populated with Kassadin text (Null Sphere, Nether Blade, Riftwalk, 'Kassadin vs Ryze' in its loading line) — that is correct for Kassadin and NOT a Galio problem, so nothing was written for it; noting only so nobody mistakes it for corruption. Galio's own Ryze entry is intact. Also: Ryze has no healing, so the 'Anti-heal if he sustains' loading line was pure filler and is gone. Galio's Justice Punch still carries a bogus derived 'terrain' flag in the kit library — no terrain claim written.
